injection_ci_offset_from: monte carlo, 3x the OTA-removed sigma at ss_mm/1.620V/125C
injection_ci_gain_error_why: the signal-dependent part of charge injection came back below the bench's resolution; the slope the fit sees is accounted for by the drawn capacitor ratio, the finite-gain leak and, at the slow/cold corners, incomplete input sampling (#106)
worst_bound_ci_offset_from: monte carlo, worst raw sample at ff_mm/1.980V/125C
worst_bound_ci_offset_caveat: NOT charge injection: the raw Monte Carlo spread is dominated by the OTA's own input-offset mismatch (r = 0.9999 against the measured vod_rst). It is carried because model B's ci_offset is any additive per-clock offset on integrator 1, so this is the honest worst case for that parameter -- its cause is simply not the switches.
worst_bound_ci_gain_error_sign: kept signed: a gain DEFICIT (negative) shrinks both integrator coefficients and is not interchangeable with an excess. This value is the incomplete input sampling of #106, not charge injection -- see worst_bound_ci_offset_caveat.
sign: ci_offset is entered as a magnitude: model B shapes it through one integrator, so the sign moves the output mean and not the in-band noise
